lead: # Runtime attestations (#doctor-reads-the-runtime) - the --runtime lens. For an IMPLEMENTATION the
# claim is LINKAGE: it runs inside someone else's module, so "linked into a closure that served" is
# what the runtime can honestly say. Execution counts are deliberately not asserted.
# The DATA GRAPH (the-data-graph-a-global-third-pillar) — `doctor` holds a node to the entities it
# declares, so it must be able to READ the entity store. One-way: bsc-data knows nothing of the
# algorithms graph.
# `default-features = false` is LOAD-BEARING, not tidiness. `bsc_data::entity` is the verbatim-JSON
# store and is NOT behind `duckdb-store`, so the two symbols this crate uses — `entity::open` and
# `entity::list` — cost nothing. With the default on, `duckdb` + `libduckdb-sys` + 11 arrow crates
# came with them, and through THIS crate they reached bsc-ui, bsc-files and bsc-component too — so
# `cargo check -p bsc-ui` compiled the bundled DuckDB C++ amalgamation (280 objects, a ~614 MB
# libduckdb.a) in a crate that has nothing to do with the data platform. Measured on a cold
# worktree, `cargo check -p bsc-ui`: 2m28s with the default, 20.8s without. plandb already did
# this; this crate was the leak.
# The shared FS-confinement gate (#3475) — `require_within_repo_root`, the CLI twin of the
# `bsc-confine` hook, so a harvest cannot read outside a confined session's root.
# `preserve_order` — LOAD-BEARING for `impl sync-seed`. The packaged seed
# (src-tauri/data/knowledge/algorithms.json) is one 6.6MB file holding every record, and its field
# order is INSERTION order, not alphabetical (verified: `JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(seed), null, 2)`
# round-trips byte-identical). Without this feature `serde_json::Value` objects are BTreeMaps, so
# parsing the whole seed and writing it back would silently re-sort every record's keys alphabetically
# — a multi-thousand-line diff for a one-field sync. With it, `Map::insert` on an EXISTING key updates
# the value in place and keeps its position, matching how `sync-impl-seed.mjs` (the script this verb
# replaces) already merged fields onto a seed record without reordering it.
# The MATERIALIZER, promoted from a dev-dependency to a real one because `repo_store` now READS the
# committed store through it (`graph_materialize::load_merged_value`). The store is being taken apart
# into `graph/records/<id>.json` (`epic-retire-json-ledgers-for-db-and-git-drivers`), and "which
# records exist" must have exactly ONE definition: the build's. A second merge implemented here could
# disagree with the compiler about what the store holds, which is the silent-divergence failure the
# split exists to remove. It stays LEAN — `serde_json` and nothing else — so this edge costs nothing.
# IT WAS A DEV-DEPENDENCY FIRST, for a separate reason that still holds
# (`graph-materialize-becomes-a-real-build-dependency`): `migrate-crate` names what it writes with
# `extract::module_id` and the build SELECTS on `plan::expected_id`, the two must agree exactly, and
# `materialize_plan_tests` proves that over every real path in the tree. Depending on the crate means
# those tests drive the SHIPPED symbols — a restatement could drift, and the drift would be invisible
# precisely where it matters.
# THE DATABASE the records are moving into (`epic-retire-json-ledgers-for-db-and-git-drivers`).
# `bsc graph store import|db` reaches it from here; the JSON ledgers stay readable until every reader
# has moved, because an import that cannot be checked against its source is not one anyone will trust.
# build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
